findings.issue_text: Federated rule groups are no longer treated as immutable: useAllRulerRuleAbilities hardcodes isFederated = false behind a TODO, so consumers delegating from the deprecated useAllAlertRuleAbilities lose the federated check, enabling destructive Edit/Delete/Pause/Restore actions on federated rules that the API will reject

returnTo param dropped from rule view URLs in GrafanaRuleListItem: createRelativeUrl('/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view') no longer includes returnTo, so navigating list to view and back loses filter/list context

useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable masks folder-fetch errors as a settled isEditable: false state: when the folder query errors, loading is false and folder is undefined, so the hook swallows the error and permanently disables menu actions indistinguishably from a legitimate RBAC denial

Cloud (datasource) rules rendered via the prom-rule-only path lose all menu actions: RuleProps allows rule to be omitted and nothing in the types enforces Grafana-list-only usage, so with non-Grafana rules rulerRule is undefined and all OR-combined abilities (canPause, canDelete, canDuplicate, canSilence, canExport) become false, emptying the More menu

useRulerRuleAbility (singular) called with possibly-undefined rule: RuleProps makes rule RulerRuleDTO | undefined but the singular hook's signature was not widened, violating the type contract and potentially throwing or producing a bad canEditRule ability value

Rules in Creating/Deleting intermediate states silently disappear from the list: GrafanaGroupLoader removed the ruler-group query and matchRules, so during the propagation window just-created rules vanish (or just-deleted rules remain) with no transitional indicator, and the deleted matchRules unit tests removed the safety net

OR-combined ability checks in AlertRuleMenu.tsx and RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx can surface destructive actions (Delete, Duplicate, Pause) where the ruler-based check denied them, due to divergence between ruler API and folder metadata permission sources (e.g., isProvisionedRule vs isProvisionedPromRule mismatches)

Silence permission check in useAbilities.ts switched from alertmanager-scoped permissions to folder-scoped permissions (useCanSilenceInFolder), allowing users with folder edit rights but no AlertingSilenceCreate grant to see and attempt silences they aren't authorized for
GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx renders only promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules, so rules in additional groups beyond the first are silently hidden from the list

RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx and AlertRuleMenu pass possibly-undefined rules into useRulerRuleAbility/useRulerRuleAbilities; downstream type guards like isProvisionedRule and isPluginProvidedRule may dereference undefined values and throw during render

Duplicate ability hook execution on every rule row: AlertRuleMenu unconditionally calls both useRulerRuleAbilities and useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities, so Grafana rule rows pay for ruler-path work including per-rule ruler-API requests, reintroducing ruler API traffic the PR claims to remove; the ruler path lacks a skipToken-style guard that the prom path has (AlertRuleMenu.tsx:56–75)

Per-rule folder fetch in useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable causes an N+1 query shape: each of ~80 rule rows mounts useFolder(rule?.folderUid) separately, creating per-row query subscriptions and permission-evaluation useMemo; a single folder-permission lookup hoisted to the group/list level would fix it (useAbilities.ts ~line 355)

Broken memoization in plural ability hooks: useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities/useRulerRuleAbilities memoize on an actions array that callers pass as inline array literals, creating a new reference every render so the useMemo never hits and ability maps recompute on every render; hoist the action arrays to module-level constants or memoize on contents (useAbilities.ts ~lines 385–395)

Federated rule support silently dropped: useAllAlertRuleAbilities now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities where isFederatedRuleGroup was replaced with `const isFederated = false` and a TODO, so federated rule groups incorrectly report Update/Delete as supported+allowed instead of NotSupported for all existing callers

Creating/Deleting transitional rule states removed from Grafana list view: ruler-API-based matching (matchRules, promOnlyRules) removed from GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx, so rules mid-deletion or newly-created rules disappear from the list under propagation lag or partial failure

Rule list item href loses the returnTo query parameter in GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx:31 (previously built via createRelativeUrl with returnTo), breaking back-navigation for users viewing a rule from the list

RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx public signature loosened: rule prop now optional and component returns null with only a logWarning when no identifier can be constructed, creating a silent-null path where previously the required-prop type system made the contract explicit
getEditableIdentifier in RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx hardcodes ruleSourceName: 'grafana' for the promRule path, so a cloud prom rule flowing in results in a silent blank instead of an error

AlertRuleMenu.tsx permission OR-logic over-grants: can* checks use (rulerSupported && rulerAllowed) || (grafanaSupported && grafanaAllowed), so if one source denies and the other (e.g., stale folder ACL metadata) allows, the menu item appears despite the denial instead of gating on either denied result

Creating/Deleting rule states silently dropped: new code renders only promResponse groups, so just-created rules (in ruler, not yet in Prometheus) are invisible and just-deleted rules disappear without a 'Deleting' state (GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx:65-77)
No polling-freshness guard; the RULE_LIST_POLL_INTERVAL_MS poll is the only thing that eventually surfaces new rules

Errors from the prom groups query are never surfaced: useGetGrafanaGroupsQuery error is not inspected, so a failed request renders the misleading generic 'no ruler rules found' Alert (GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx:48-65)

useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable conflates fetch failure with 'not editable': when useFolder errors, the hook permanently returns { isEditable: false, isRemovable: false, loading: false }, silently revoking edit permissions until remount (useAbilities.ts ~345-370)

isPluginProvidedRule(rule) and rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule) called on a possibly-undefined rule inside memo in useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities; skipToken path passes undefined and could crash the component tree (useAbilities.ts ~293-295)

Deleted GrafanaRuleLoader removes per-rule error handling in FilterView; new GrafanaRuleListItem has no not-found/deleted-mid-session handling, and non-optional destructuring of name, uid, labels, provenance will throw if rule fields are missing (FilterView.tsx:154-162)
RuleActionsButtons returns null when identifier construction fails, silently hiding all actions with no UI explanation (RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx ~60-63)
Silence ability drops the alertmanager-availability check from useCanSilence, potentially rendering a Silence action that fails on click (useAbilities.ts ~288-320)
Stray '// duplicate' comment on useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable looks like leftover copy-paste annotation; worth cleaning

RulesTable RBAC tests mock away the useAbilities module entirely, so the new OR-combination logic (canX = (ruler && ruler) || (grafana && grafana)) in AlertRuleMenu/RuleActionsButtons is never executed; tests should use MSW-backed permission responses to exercise the real logic

No unit tests exist for the new useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities hook's silence/export semantics changes (folder-permission-based silencing, recording rules not silenceable, non-alerting rules losing Pause/Export/Restore)

matchRules tests for ruler-only ('Creating') and prom-only ('Deleting') rules were deleted without replacement; GrafanaGroupLoader now renders only prom rules, silently hiding ruler-only rules, with no test asserting this new contract
skipToken handling in useAbilities.ts is untested — no test verifies that a datasource/cloud rule does not accidentally get grafana-prom abilities in AlertRuleMenu/RuleActionsButtons

GrafanaGroupLoader tests grant full permissions but never test the negative case that menu items (delete, export, etc.) are absent when permissions are denied under the new folder-metadata-based permission model

useAllRulerRuleAbilities in useAbilities.ts hardcodes isFederated = false instead of computing isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group), silently breaking federated-rule immutability for callers of the deprecated useAllAlertRuleAbilities wrapper; federated rules now incorrectly show Edit/Delete as supported+allowed (TODO comment not preserving behavior)

useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities is a near-verbatim copy of useAllRulerRuleAbilities, duplicating the entire RBAC abilities matrix so every future ability change must be made twice; shared abilities-computation should be extracted into a parameterized helper
useAbilities.ts defines a local skipToken symbol instead of reusing RTK Query's exported skipToken, creating two incompatible 'skip' conventions in the same codebase and a type-boundary leak

AlertRuleMenu.tsx passes the actions array inline to useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities, so the fresh array literal every render defeats the hook's useMemo and causes per-render hook churn; the array should be hoisted to a module-level constant (same risk applies to useRulerRuleAbilities)

AlertRuleMenu.tsx hand-rolls the OR-combination pattern canX = (aSupported && aAllowed) || (bSupported && bAllowed) five times (Pause, Delete, Duplicate, Silence, Export), embedding authoritative-source policy in a presentational component; the decision should live in a single abilities-layer hook, and list views without ruler data trigger extra ability requests per rule

RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx getEditableIdentifier returns undefined for unidentifiable rules, causing the component to return null and silently lose all action buttons (delete/duplicate/silence/export) with no user-visible error; also ruleId.fromRulerRuleAndGroupIdentifierV2 can throw in some versions but the acknowledged try/catch is missing

GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx removed matchRules edge-case tests (unmatched prom rules, ruler-only rules) and Creating/Deleting list-item tests without replacing them, leaving only happy-path coverage and regressing test coverage for behavior that still exists

RulesTable.test.tsx mocks assert against implementation details with duplicated mockImplementation blocks for singular/plural hook variants, mocking hooks never called and losing the ability to pin down which hook the component actually calls (mock/test drift hazard); a single beforeEach action-keyed helper could serve all tests

GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx has dead code: the operation prop and RuleOperation import are unused after matchRules removal, and optional-chaining guards in commonProps (rule?.health) are dead since rule is non-optional in the props type

RuleDetails.test.tsx executes mimirDataSource() at module scope, coupling test file load order to mock state that jest.clearAllMocks() in beforeAll cannot reset; it should be constructed inside the describe/test that needs it

Permission escalation via OR-union of two ability sources in AlertRuleMenu.tsx and RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx: canDelete unions folder-metadata and ruler API authorization sources, resolving disagreements to the most permissive answer for destructive actions; should be intersection or exclusively selected

Federated-rule protection silently dropped: useAllAlertRuleAbilities hardcodes isFederated = false with a TODO, making federated Mimir rule groups fully editable/deletable (regression from old isFederatedRuleGroup check)

Ruler/prom reconciliation deleted in GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx: ruler-only rules (creating state) disappear from list, and prom-only rules (being deleted) render as normal rules with full Edit/Delete menus
Tests covering creating/deleting states and matchRules in GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx were deleted, not migrated, removing coverage that would catch the reconciliation regression

Rules without a folderUid are silently stripped of all edit/delete permissions in useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable: missing folderUid returns isEditable:false with loading:false, indistinguishable from a permission denial with no error surfaced

Folder-metadata permission check (hasPermissionInMetadata) in useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable may deny org-level or basic-role AlertingRuleUpdate grants that have no per-folder metadata entry; the new test only passes because the mock explicitly injects folder access control metadata

RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx returns null for any non-Grafana prom-only rule: getEditableIdentifier fails and the entire action row silently renders nothing, with logWarning going to analytics rather than the user

Loading-state race on Silence ability in useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities: no loading gating on the Silence tuple, so the menu item can flicker in/out and a not-yet-settled prom-side check can enable Silence for unsupported rules
returnTo query param dropped from rule view links in GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx, breaking back-navigation context from the list view

Test-side meta-issue: all ability hooks are jest.mocked wholesale with both sources mocked to the same values, making the OR-union logic, ability-source disagreement, and undefined-folder/no-folderUid paths structurally untestable

goldens.comment: The rendered GrafanaRuleListItem is missing the required key prop for React list items. This can cause rendering issues when the list order changes.

RuleActionsButtons is invoked with only promRule, but SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer inside RuleActionsButtons still depends on a Grafana Ruler rule being present, so for Grafana rules coming from list views the 'Silence notifications' menu entry (now driven by Grafana Prom abilities) will toggle showSilenceDrawer without ever rendering the drawer. This means clicking 'Silence notifications' for these rules has no visible effect, even when abilities indicate silencing is allowed.

RuleActionsButtons is invoked with only promRule, but SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer inside RuleActionsButtons still depends on a Grafana Ruler rule being present, so for Grafana rules coming from list views the 'Silence notifications' menu entry (now driven by Grafana Prom abilities) will toggle showSilenceDrawer without ever rendering the drawer. This means clicking 'Silence notifications' for these rules has no visible effect, even when abilities indicate silencing is allowed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Federated rule groups are no longer treated as immutable: useAllRulerRuleAbilities hardcodes isFederated = false behind a TODO, so consumers delegating from the deprecated useAllAlertRuleAbilities lose the federated check, enabling destructive Edit/Delete/Pause/Restore actions on federated rules that the API will reject

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes federated immutability handling in the abilities calculation. Previously, `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` computed `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` (via the old import), and used it in `immutableRule = isProvisioned || isFederated || isPluginProvided` to disable destructive actions. In the refactor, `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` now delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, and `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` explicitly hardcodes `const isFederated = false` with a TODO, meaning federated rules are no longer treated as immutable and can surface Edit/Delete/Pause/Restore as supported/allowed when they should be blocked.

adjudication_records.issue_text: returnTo param dropped from rule view URLs in GrafanaRuleListItem: createRelativeUrl('/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view') no longer includes returnTo, so navigating list to view and back loses filter/list context

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the prior `createReturnTo()` usage and no longer passes `{ returnTo }` into `createRelativeUrl` for Grafana rule view links. In the deleted `GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx`, the href was `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })`, but in the new `GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx` it is `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`)`. This is a verifiable regression that would drop the return/list context parameter when navigating from the list to the rule view.

adjudication_records.issue_text: useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable masks folder-fetch errors as a settled isEditable: false state: when the folder query errors, loading is false and folder is undefined, so the hook swallows the error and permanently disables menu actions indistinguishably from a legitimate RBAC denial

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable()` in `useAbilities.ts`, which only consumes `{ folder, loading } = useFolder(folderUID)` and returns `{ isEditable: false, isRemovable: false, loading }` whenever `folder` is falsy. There is no propagation of a folder-fetch error state (no `error` value is consulted or returned), so if `useFolder` resolves with `folder === undefined` and `loading === false` due to an error, the hook will present the same settled “not editable/removable” state as a legitimate RBAC denial. This is a concrete, diff-grounded edge case/observability concern, though the diff alone doesn’t prove `useFolder` behaves exactly as described on error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cloud (datasource) rules rendered via the prom-rule-only path lose all menu actions: RuleProps allows rule to be omitted and nothing in the types enforces Grafana-list-only usage, so with non-Grafana rules rulerRule is undefined and all OR-combined abilities (canPause, canDelete, canDuplicate, canSilence, canExport) become false, emptying the More menu

adjudication.rationale: The diff’s “prom-rule-only” rendering path is introduced specifically for Grafana-managed rules (GrafanaGroupLoader now only uses prometheusApi and GrafanaRuleListItem passes only promRule for Grafana rules). The datasource/cloud path in FilterView remains handled by DataSourceRuleLoader, and the tests explicitly model cloud rules as relying on useRulerRuleAbilities while useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities receives skipToken. Nothing in this diff shows Cloud/datasource rules being rendered without a rulerRule such that AlertRuleMenu would lose actions; the scenario described is not verifiable from the changes shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: useRulerRuleAbility (singular) called with possibly-undefined rule: RuleProps makes rule RulerRuleDTO | undefined but the singular hook's signature was not widened, violating the type contract and potentially throwing or producing a bad canEditRule ability value

adjudication.rationale: In RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx, Props were changed so `rule` is optional (RequireAtLeastOne with `rule?: RulerRuleDTO`), and the new GrafanaRuleListItem calls `<RuleActionsButtons promRule={rule} ... />` without providing `rule`, making `rule` undefined at runtime. However the component still calls `useRulerRuleAbility(rule, groupIdentifier, AlertRuleAction.Update)` with that possibly-undefined value. In useAbilities.ts, only the *plural* `useRulerRuleAbilities` was widened to accept `RulerRuleDTO | undefined`; the diff shows no widening for the singular `useRulerRuleAbility`, so this violates the hook’s type contract and risks incorrect ability evaluation or runtime errors inside the hook.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Rules in Creating/Deleting intermediate states silently disappear from the list: GrafanaGroupLoader removed the ruler-group query and matchRules, so during the propagation window just-created rules vanish (or just-deleted rules remain) with no transitional indicator, and the deleted matchRules unit tests removed the safety net

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly removes GrafanaGroupLoader’s ruler-group query and the reconciliation logic (`useGetGrafanaRulerGroupQuery`, `matchRules`, and rendering of `RuleOperationListItem` for `RuleOperation.Deleting`, plus the “creating” branch when a ruler rule had no matching prom rule). The new implementation in `GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx` renders only `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules`, so the UI no longer has any way to show ruler-only “creating” rules or prom-only “deleting” rules, and the unit tests for `matchRules` were deleted. Whether this is an actual runtime bug depends on an unverified assumption about strong consistency between the APIs, but the loss of intermediate-state handling is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: OR-combined ability checks in AlertRuleMenu.tsx and RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx can surface destructive actions (Delete, Duplicate, Pause) where the ruler-based check denied them, due to divergence between ruler API and folder metadata permission sources (e.g., isProvisionedRule vs isProvisionedPromRule mismatches)

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes permission gating to OR-combine abilities from two different sources. In AlertRuleMenu.tsx, canDelete/canDuplicate/canPause/etc are computed as `(rulerSupported && rulerAllowed) || (grafanaSupported && grafanaAllowed)`. In RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx, canEditRule is similarly OR-combined between `useRulerRuleAbility(...)` and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility(...)`. Because the two ability systems use different “immutability” inputs (e.g., ruler provisioning uses `isProvisionedRule(rule)` based on `rulerRule.grafana_alert.provenance`, while prom provisioning uses `isProvisionedPromRule(promRule)` based on optional `promRule.provenance` newly added in the DTO), they can diverge and the OR logic will show actions if either side allows, even when the other side would deny (e.g., a provisioned rule where prom provenance is missing/lagging). This is a verifiable change in the diff that can surface destructive UI actions contrary to the stricter check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Silence permission check in useAbilities.ts switched from alertmanager-scoped permissions to folder-scoped permissions (useCanSilenceInFolder), allowing users with folder edit rights but no AlertingSilenceCreate grant to see and attempt silences they aren't authorized for

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a change in `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` from `useCanSilence(rule)` to `useCanSilenceInFolder(rule?.folderUid)` and adds `silenceSupported = useGrafanaRulesSilenceSupport()`, but it does not show the implementation of `useCanSilenceInFolder`. Therefore the claim that the new logic “allows users with folder edit rights but no AlertingSilenceCreate grant” cannot be verified from this PR diff alone. The only visible permission references around silence are the new hooks and the updated tests explicitly granting `AccessControlAction.AlertingSilenceCreate`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx renders only promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules, so rules in additional groups beyond the first are silently hidden from the list

adjudication.rationale: In `GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx`, the render path iterates only `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules` (previously it at least computed `promRules` the same way but still rendered based on `rulerResponse?.rules`). Since `useGetGrafanaGroupsQuery` returns a `groups` array and other code in the diff (the deleted `GrafanaRuleLoader`) used `promRuleGroup?.data.groups.flatMap((group) => group.rules)`, limiting to `.at(0)` will omit any rules returned in additional groups, effectively hiding them from the list.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx and AlertRuleMenu pass possibly-undefined rules into useRulerRuleAbility/useRulerRuleAbilities; downstream type guards like isProvisionedRule and isPluginProvidedRule may dereference undefined values and throw during render

adjudication.rationale:
The diff introduces code paths where `rule` can be `undefined`:
- `GrafanaRuleListItem` renders `<RuleActionsButtons promRule={rule} ... />` without a `rule` (ruler) prop, but `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx` still calls `useRulerRuleAbility(rule, groupIdentifier, ...)`, so the hook may receive `undefined`.
- In `useAbilities.ts`, `useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule: RulerRuleDTO | undefined, ...)` now allows `rule` to be undefined and then calls `isPluginProvidedRule(rule)` (and similarly `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` calls `isPluginProvidedRule(rule)`) without an explicit undefined guard.
Whether this actually throws depends on implementations not shown in the diff (e.g., `useRulerRuleAbility`, `isPluginProvidedRule`), so it’s not a verifiable runtime bug from the diff alone, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded edge case that should be validated/handled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate ability hook execution on every rule row: AlertRuleMenu unconditionally calls both useRulerRuleAbilities and useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities, so Grafana rule rows pay for ruler-path work including per-rule ruler-API requests, reintroducing ruler API traffic the PR claims to remove; the ruler path lacks a skipToken-style guard that the prom path has (AlertRuleMenu.tsx:56–75)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows AlertRuleMenu now *always* invokes both hooks: `useRulerRuleAbilities(rulerRule, groupIdentifier, [...])` and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(..., [...])` (AlertRuleMenu.tsx). Only the Prom hook is guarded with `skipToken`; the ruler-path call has no equivalent conditional and will run even when the component is used from the list view where `rulerRule` may be `undefined` (the hook signature was changed to accept `RulerRuleDTO | undefined`). Whether that necessarily reintroduces per-row Ruler API traffic cannot be verified from this diff alone (depends on internals of `useIsRuleEditable`/other hooks), but the duplicated hook execution/possible unnecessary work is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Per-rule folder fetch in useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable causes an N+1 query shape: each of ~80 rule rows mounts useFolder(rule?.folderUid) separately, creating per-row query subscriptions and permission-evaluation useMemo; a single folder-permission lookup hoisted to the group/list level would fix it (useAbilities.ts ~line 355)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable()` in `useAbilities.ts`, which calls `useFolder(rule?.folderUid)` per invocation. This hook is used by `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities()`, which is in turn used by `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility/Abilities()`. The list UI mounts these per rule row (e.g., `RuleActionsButtons.V2` calls `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility(...)`, and `AlertRuleMenu` calls `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(...)`), so rendering ~80 rules will create ~80 `useFolder(...)` subscriptions / permission computations. This is a performance/architecture issue (N+1 shape), not a direct functional defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Broken memoization in plural ability hooks: useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities/useRulerRuleAbilities memoize on an actions array that callers pass as inline array literals, creating a new reference every render so the useMemo never hits and ability maps recompute on every render; hoist the action arrays to module-level constants or memoize on contents (useAbilities.ts ~lines 385–395)

adjudication.rationale: The plural hooks do `useMemo(() => actions.map(...), [abilities, actions])` in `useRulerRuleAbilities` and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` (useAbilities.ts). In `AlertRuleMenu.tsx`, both hooks are called with inline array literals of actions, so `actions` is a new reference each render and the memoized mapping will recompute every render. This is a performance/memoization concern (the mapping memo never hits), not a functional correctness defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Federated rule support silently dropped: useAllAlertRuleAbilities now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities where isFederatedRuleGroup was replaced with `const isFederated = false` and a TODO, so federated rule groups incorrectly report Update/Delete as supported+allowed instead of NotSupported for all existing callers

adjudication.rationale: In `useAbilities.ts`, `useAllAlertRuleAbilities()` now delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities(rule.rulerRule, groupIdentifierV2)`. Inside `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, the prior federated check is removed and replaced with `const isFederated = false; // TODO: Add support for federated rules`, and `isFederatedRuleGroup` is no longer imported/used. Since `immutableRule` is computed from `isProvisioned || isFederated || isPluginProvided`, federated rules that were previously treated as immutable will now be treated as mutable, affecting Update/Delete/Pause/Restore/DeletePermanently support/allow decisions for callers of these hooks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Creating/Deleting transitional rule states removed from Grafana list view: ruler-API-based matching (matchRules, promOnlyRules) removed from GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx, so rules mid-deletion or newly-created rules disappear from the list under propagation lag or partial failure

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly removes the ruler-API fetch and matching logic from `GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx` (deleted `useGetGrafanaRulerGroupQuery`, `matchRules`, `promOnlyRules`, and rendering of `RuleOperationListItem` for `RuleOperation.Deleting`; also removes the `Creating` branch when a ruler rule has no prom match). The new implementation renders only `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules`, so any rule that exists only in the ruler response (newly created but not yet in Prom) or only in Prom (deleted in ruler but not yet propagated) will no longer appear with transitional UI. Whether this is a true bug depends on guarantees about consistency/propagation, which the diff does not prove either way.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Rule list item href loses the returnTo query parameter in GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx:31 (previously built via createRelativeUrl with returnTo), breaking back-navigation for users viewing a rule from the list

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that the previous implementation (deleted GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx) built the rule link with `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })` where `returnTo` came from `createReturnTo()`. The new `GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx` constructs `href` as `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`)` with no `returnTo` parameter. This is a concrete behavior change visible in the diff and would remove the back-navigation context previously preserved via `returnTo`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx public signature loosened: rule prop now optional and component returns null with only a logWarning when no identifier can be constructed, creating a silent-null path where previously the required-prop type system made the contract explicit

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx props from a required `rule: RulerRuleDTO` to `RequireAtLeastOne<{ rule?: RulerRuleDTO; promRule?: Rule; }>` and adds a guard: `const identifier = getEditableIdentifier(...); if (!identifier) { return null; }`. `getEditableIdentifier` logs a warning and returns `undefined` when only `promRule` is provided but it is not a Grafana prom rule (`if (prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule)) { ... } else { logWarning(...); return undefined; }`). This introduces a new silent-null rendering path compared to the previous always-required `rule` contract. It’s not a verifiable runtime defect in this diff, but it is a real contract/diagnostics concern created by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getEditableIdentifier in RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx hardcodes ruleSourceName: 'grafana' for the promRule path, so a cloud prom rule flowing in results in a silent blank instead of an error

adjudication.rationale: In RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx, getEditableIdentifier only returns `{ ruleSourceName: 'grafana', uid: promRule.uid }` when `prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule)` is true. A “cloud prom rule” (non-Grafana prom rule) would not satisfy that predicate, so it would not be mislabeled as `ruleSourceName: 'grafana'`; instead it hits the fallback path that logs a warning and returns `undefined`, causing the component to return `null`. The finding’s claim that a cloud prom rule would flow through this hardcoded grafana path is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AlertRuleMenu.tsx permission OR-logic over-grants: can* checks use (rulerSupported && rulerAllowed) || (grafanaSupported && grafanaAllowed), so if one source denies and the other (e.g., stale folder ACL metadata) allows, the menu item appears despite the denial instead of gating on either denied result

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce the described OR-combination in AlertRuleMenu.tsx (e.g., `canDelete = (deleteSupported && deleteAllowed) || (grafanaDeleteSupported && grafanaDeleteAllowed)`), so it is true that a denial from one ability source can be overridden by an allow from the other. However, the diff also explicitly documents the intent to use prom-rule abilities for list-view consumers (no Ruler API calls), and the diff alone does not establish the correct precedence/aggregation semantics (fallback vs. union). So the concern is real and diff-grounded, but it’s not verifiably a defect without additional specification of intended RBAC behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Creating/Deleting rule states silently dropped: new code renders only promResponse groups, so just-created rules (in ruler, not yet in Prometheus) are invisible and just-deleted rules disappear without a 'Deleting' state (GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx:65-77)

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes fetching/using the Ruler group in `GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx` and deletes the `matchRules` logic plus the rendering of `RuleOperationListItem` for `RuleOperation.Deleting` and the `RuleOperation.Creating` path. The new implementation only renders `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules` (lines ~65-77 in the new file), so any ruler-only rules (previously shown as "Creating") and prom-only rules (previously shown as "Deleting") will no longer be rendered at all. This matches the finding that the creating/deleting transient states are silently dropped.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No polling-freshness guard; the RULE_LIST_POLL_INTERVAL_MS poll is the only thing that eventually surfaces new rules

adjudication.rationale: In GrafanaGroupLoader the component now only fetches Grafana rules via prometheusApi.useGetGrafanaGroupsQuery with { pollingInterval: RULE_LIST_POLL_INTERVAL_MS } and no longer queries the ruler API nor matches ruler-only rules (creating) / prom-only rules (deleting). Additionally, prometheusGroupsGenerator removed prefetching alertRuleApi.getGrafanaRulerGroup. This means discovery of newly created/updated rules (or temporary inconsistencies) relies on the periodic poll/refetch, with no additional freshness/consistency mechanism in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Errors from the prom groups query are never surfaced: useGetGrafanaGroupsQuery error is not inspected, so a failed request renders the misleading generic 'no ruler rules found' Alert (GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx:48-65)

adjudication.rationale: In GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx the previous error handling for the Prometheus query was removed. The code now only checks `isPromResponseLoading` and then `if (!promResponse)` renders a generic Alert, but it never inspects/branches on `useGetGrafanaGroupsQuery`'s `error` field. Therefore a failed `useGetGrafanaGroupsQuery` request will fall into the `!promResponse` path and show a misleading “no rules found”/generic message instead of surfacing the request failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable conflates fetch failure with 'not editable': when useFolder errors, the hook permanently returns { isEditable: false, isRemovable: false, loading: false }, silently revoking edit permissions until remount (useAbilities.ts ~345-370)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable()` which only consumes `{ folder, loading } = useFolder(folderUID)` and treats `!folder` as "Loading or invalid folder UID", returning `{ isEditable: false, isRemovable: false, loading }` (and if `loading` is false, it becomes a silent deny). There is no explicit error path or surfaced error state in this hook, so a folder-fetch failure would be indistinguishable from lack of permissions/invalid folder and would suppress edit/delete actions without explanation. However, claims about it being "permanent until remount" cannot be verified from this diff because `useFolder`’s error/retry behavior isn’t shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isPluginProvidedRule(rule) and rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule) called on a possibly-undefined rule inside memo in useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities; skipToken path passes undefined and could crash the component tree (useAbilities.ts ~293-295)

adjudication.rationale: In useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities (useAbilities.ts), the memo does call isPluginProvidedRule(rule) with rule typed as GrafanaPromRuleDTO | undefined (skipToken path maps to undefined). However, the finding specifically claims both isPluginProvidedRule(rule) and rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule) are called there; in the shown diff, useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities does not call rulerRuleType.grafana.rule at all (it uses prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) instead). Also, whether isPluginProvidedRule / prometheusRuleType guards crash on undefined cannot be verified from this diff alone (their implementations aren’t shown), and similar patterns exist elsewhere in the file, suggesting these helpers may be designed to tolerate undefined.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Deleted GrafanaRuleLoader removes per-rule error handling in FilterView; new GrafanaRuleListItem has no not-found/deleted-mid-session handling, and non-optional destructuring of name, uid, labels, provenance will throw if rule fields are missing (FilterView.tsx:154-162)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the per-rule fetch/error states that existed in the deleted `GrafanaRuleLoader` (it handled `rulerRuleGroupError || promRuleGroupError`, loading skeletons, and an explicit “Cannot find rule details for UID …” error alert). In `FilterView.tsx`, Grafana items are now rendered directly via `GrafanaRuleListItem rule={rule}` with no analogous not-found/error UI, so mid-session deletion/inconsistency would no longer surface as a per-item error message. However, the claim that `const { name, uid, labels, provenance } = rule;` will throw if fields are missing is incorrect—only `rule` being `null/undefined` would throw, and missing properties simply become `undefined`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RuleActionsButtons returns null when identifier construction fails, silently hiding all actions with no UI explanation (RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx ~60-63)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce this behavior: in RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx, `const identifier = getEditableIdentifier(...)` is followed by `if (!identifier) { return null; }`, and `getEditableIdentifier` can return `undefined` (it logs `logWarning('Unable to construct an editable rule identifier')`). That would hide the entire action button/menu UI with no user-facing explanation. However, this is a defensive fallback for unexpected inputs (commented as safer than throwing) and is not clearly a verifiable functional defect from the diff alone, since normal call sites shown (e.g., GrafanaRuleListItem passes a Grafana promRule) should produce an identifier.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Silence ability drops the alertmanager-availability check from useCanSilence, potentially rendering a Silence action that fails on click (useAbilities.ts ~288-320)

adjudication.rationale: In `useAbilities.ts`, the new `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities()` computes `AlertRuleAction.Silence` as `[silenceSupported, canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule]` and no longer uses the prior `useCanSilence(rule)` path that `useAllRulerRuleAbilities()` uses. This is a real, diff-grounded behavior change: silence gating for Grafana Prom rules is now delegated to `useGrafanaRulesSilenceSupport()`/`useCanSilenceInFolder()`. Whether this actually drops an alertmanager-availability check (and causes a click-time failure) depends on implementations not shown in the diff, so the “fails on click” part isn’t verifiable here, but the potential regression risk is concrete.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stray '// duplicate' comment on useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable looks like leftover copy-paste annotation; worth cleaning

adjudication.rationale: The diff does include an inline comment `// duplicate` on the line `const { isEditable, isRemovable, loading } = useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable(rule); // duplicate` in `useAbilities.ts`, but this is a minor style/cleanup nit rather than a specific nontrivial review issue or a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RulesTable RBAC tests mock away the useAbilities module entirely, so the new OR-combination logic (canX = (ruler && ruler) || (grafana && grafana)) in AlertRuleMenu/RuleActionsButtons is never executed; tests should use MSW-backed permission responses to exercise the real logic

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `RulesTable.test.tsx` does `jest.mock('../../hooks/useAbilities')`, but the new OR-combination logic in `AlertRuleMenu.tsx` and `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx` is still executed at render time using the mocked hook return values (e.g., `canDelete = (deleteSupported && deleteAllowed) || (grafanaDeleteSupported && grafanaDeleteAllowed)`). The tests may not be exercising real RBAC/permission fetching, but it is false that the OR logic is “never executed” just because the hooks are mocked.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No unit tests exist for the new useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities hook's silence/export semantics changes (folder-permission-based silencing, recording rules not silenceable, non-alerting rules losing Pause/Export/Restore)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new nontrivial ability logic in `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` (`useAbilities.ts`), changing semantics such as `Silence` being `[silenceSupported, canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule]` and `ModifyExport/Pause/Restore/DeletePermanently` being gated by `isAlertingRule` (so non-alerting/recording rules lose those abilities). The updated tests (`GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx`, `RulesTable.test.tsx`) mainly mock abilities or assert menu items appear for a Grafana alerting rule with broad permissions; they do not directly unit-test the new hook’s behavior for recording/non-alerting rules or the folder-permission-based silencing/export/pause gating. This is a specific, diff-grounded missing-test issue rather than a proven runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: matchRules tests for ruler-only ('Creating') and prom-only ('Deleting') rules were deleted without replacement; GrafanaGroupLoader now renders only prom rules, silently hiding ruler-only rules, with no test asserting this new contract

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes `matchRules` and its tests (GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx deletes the whole `describe('matchRules'...)` and the previous tests that asserted 'Creating' (ruler-only) and 'Deleting' (prom-only) UI). In `GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx`, the component no longer queries ruler groups and now renders only `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules.map(...)`, with the previous branches for ruler-only and `promOnlyRules` deletion list items removed. This means any ruler-only/prom-only divergence would no longer be represented or asserted by tests; the PR relies on an implicit new contract (strong consistency) without a test/documented assertion of that behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: skipToken handling in useAbilities.ts is untested — no test verifies that a datasource/cloud rule does not accidentally get grafana-prom abilities in AlertRuleMenu/RuleActionsButtons

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new skipToken-based branching to prevent applying Grafana Prom rule abilities to non-Grafana rules (e.g., `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule) ? promRule : skipToken, ...)` in `AlertRuleMenu.tsx` and similar in `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx`). While tests were updated with comments noting that cloud rules should get `skipToken`, the tests do not explicitly verify the skipToken path by making Grafana-prom abilities return `true` and asserting they do *not* affect cloud/datasource rules (they mostly rely on default neutral mocks). So the finding about missing targeted test coverage for this new nontrivial gating logic is grounded, but it’s not a verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GrafanaGroupLoader tests grant full permissions but never test the negative case that menu items (delete, export, etc.) are absent when permissions are denied under the new folder-metadata-based permission model

adjudication.rationale: In GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx a beforeEach grants broad user permissions via grantUserPermissions(...) and folder-metadata permissions via setFolderAccessControl({...: true}). The new tests then assert the More-menu shows items (silence/duplicate/copy link/export) when permissions are granted (e.g. "should render correct menu actions when More button is clicked"). There is only one negative-permissions test, and it checks only that the Edit button is absent when folder update/delete are set false ("should not render edit button when user lacks edit permissions"); it does not verify that menu items like Duplicate/Export/Silence are hidden when corresponding permissions are denied under the folder-metadata-based model newly introduced in useAbilities.ts (useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable + folder metadata checks). This is a specific, diff-grounded missing-test gap, not an immediate functional defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: useAllRulerRuleAbilities in useAbilities.ts hardcodes isFederated = false instead of computing isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group), silently breaking federated-rule immutability for callers of the deprecated useAllAlertRuleAbilities wrapper; federated rules now incorrectly show Edit/Delete as supported+allowed (TODO comment not preserving behavior)

adjudication.rationale: In useAbilities.ts, the new useAllRulerRuleAbilities() computes `immutableRule` using `const isFederated = false` with a TODO, whereas previously federated immutability was enforced via `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` in the old useAllAlertRuleAbilities implementation. The deprecated wrapper useAllAlertRuleAbilities now just delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities and therefore no longer applies federated-rule-group immutability at all, meaning federated rules can become "supported" for Update/Delete/etc when they should be NotSupported.

adjudication_records.issue_text: useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities is a near-verbatim copy of useAllRulerRuleAbilities, duplicating the entire RBAC abilities matrix so every future ability change must be made twice; shared abilities-computation should be extracted into a parameterized helper

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new hook `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` in `useAbilities.ts` that reimplements an abilities map very similar in shape to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`: it builds an `Abilities<AlertRuleAction>` object with the same action keys (Duplicate/Create/Update/Delete/Explore/Silence/ModifyExport/Pause/Restore/DeletePermanently) and similar “immutable/provisioned/plugin-provided” gating logic. Although there are some GrafanaProm-specific differences (e.g., `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable`, `getRulesPermissions('grafana')`, `useGrafanaRulesSilenceSupport`, `prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule`), the RBAC/abilities matrix is effectively duplicated across two functions, meaning future changes to action support/permissions would likely need to be applied in both places. This is a concrete maintainability/architecture issue grounded in the newly introduced code, not a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: useAbilities.ts defines a local skipToken symbol instead of reusing RTK Query's exported skipToken, creating two incompatible 'skip' conventions in the same codebase and a type-boundary leak

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new exported sentinel `export const skipToken = Symbol('ability-skip-token')` in `useAbilities.ts` and uses it from components (e.g., `AlertRuleMenu.tsx`, `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx`) to conditionally disable ability checks. While this isn’t a correctness defect by itself, the name `skipToken` overlaps with RTK Query’s well-known `skipToken` concept and could cause architectural/confusion issues (accidental wrong import, two different sentinels with the same name). The claim that this creates “two incompatible skip conventions in the codebase” can’t be fully verified from the diff alone, but the potential for convention collision is directly introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AlertRuleMenu.tsx passes the actions array inline to useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities, so the fresh array literal every render defeats the hook's useMemo and causes per-render hook churn; the array should be hoisted to a module-level constant (same risk applies to useRulerRuleAbilities)

adjudication.rationale: In AlertRuleMenu.tsx the calls to useRulerRuleAbilities(..., [AlertRuleAction.Pause, ...]) and useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(..., [AlertRuleAction.Pause, ...]) pass an inline array literal each render. In useAbilities.ts, useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities (and similarly useRulerRuleAbilities) memoize the mapped result with `useMemo(..., [abilities, actions])`, so a new `actions` array reference will cause the memo to recompute every render. This is a diff-grounded performance/memoization issue, not a functional bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AlertRuleMenu.tsx hand-rolls the OR-combination pattern canX = (aSupported && aAllowed) || (bSupported && bAllowed) five times (Pause, Delete, Duplicate, Silence, Export), embedding authoritative-source policy in a presentational component; the decision should live in a single abilities-layer hook, and list views without ruler data trigger extra ability requests per rule

adjudication.rationale: In AlertRuleMenu.tsx the diff introduces two parallel ability sources (useRulerRuleAbilities and useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities) and then computes canPause/canDelete/canDuplicate/canSilence/canExport by repeating the pattern `(rulerSupported && rulerAllowed) || (grafanaSupported && grafanaAllowed)` five times. This hard-codes the “authoritative source” merge policy inside a UI/presentational component rather than encapsulating it in the abilities layer (e.g., a single hook returning merged abilities). The claim about list views triggering extra per-rule ability requests is only partially verifiable: the component now always invokes both ability hooks (even if promRule is skipToken / rulerRule is undefined), which can increase work, but the diff alone doesn’t prove additional network requests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx getEditableIdentifier returns undefined for unidentifiable rules, causing the component to return null and silently lose all action buttons (delete/duplicate/silence/export) with no user-visible error; also ruleId.fromRulerRuleAndGroupIdentifierV2 can throw in some versions but the acknowledged try/catch is missing

adjudication.rationale: In RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx, getEditableIdentifier can return undefined (when only promRule is provided and it is not a Grafana prom rule), and the component then `return null;` (line added after `if (!identifier)`). That would remove *all* action UI (edit + menu) with only a `logWarning` and no user-visible fallback, which is a concrete edge-case/robustness concern introduced by changing Props to allow `rule` to be absent. However, the claim that `ruleId.fromRulerRuleAndGroupIdentifierV2` can throw is not verifiable from this diff alone (no evidence of throwing behavior shown).

adjudication_records.issue_text: GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx removed matchRules edge-case tests (unmatched prom rules, ruler-only rules) and Creating/Deleting list-item tests without replacing them, leaving only happy-path coverage and regressing test coverage for behavior that still exists

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the underlying behavior entirely: GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx no longer queries the Ruler API, deletes the matchRules helper and its logic, and deletes rendering of Creating/Deleting list items (promOnlyRules/RuleOperationListItem). GrafanaGroupLoader now renders only promResponse rules. Therefore, removing the matchRules edge-case tests and Creating/Deleting tests is consistent with the code change; the finding’s claim that this behavior “still exists” is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RulesTable.test.tsx mocks assert against implementation details with duplicated mockImplementation blocks for singular/plural hook variants, mocking hooks never called and losing the ability to pin down which hook the component actually calls (mock/test drift hazard); a single beforeEach action-keyed helper could serve all tests

adjudication.rationale: In `RulesTable.test.tsx`, the diff expands mocking to both singular and plural variants (`useRulerRuleAbility`, `useRulerRuleAbilities`, `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility`, `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`) and then repeatedly sets per-test `mockImplementation` for different hook shapes (e.g., Grafana-rule tests mock `useAlertRuleAbility` plus `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, while defaults in `beforeEach` also mock several hooks). This is test-architecture/maintainability debt: it increases coupling to internal hook choices and risks mock/test drift if components switch between singular/plural hooks. It’s not a product defect, but a concrete, diff-grounded review concern about over-mocking and duplicated mocking patterns that could be consolidated with an action-keyed helper.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx has dead code: the operation prop and RuleOperation import are unused after matchRules removal, and optional-chaining guards in commonProps (rule?.health) are dead since rule is non-optional in the props type

adjudication.rationale: In the new GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx, the `operation` prop is still used: it is passed through to `<AlertRuleListItem ... operation={operation} />`, and `RuleOperation` is used in the prop type (`operation?: RuleOperation`), so neither is dead code. Also, while `rule` is non-optional in the props, the optional chaining in `commonProps` (e.g., `rule?.health`) is merely redundant, not dead/unreachable code or a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RuleDetails.test.tsx executes mimirDataSource() at module scope, coupling test file load order to mock state that jest.clearAllMocks() in beforeAll cannot reset; it should be constructed inside the describe/test that needs it

adjudication.rationale: In RuleDetails.test.tsx the diff adds `const { dataSource: mimirDs } = mimirDataSource();` at module scope (outside any `describe`/`it`), and then uses it in the test (`getCloudRule(..., { rulesSource: mimirDs })`). This does create shared state at import time that is not affected by `jest.clearAllMocks()` in `beforeAll`, so the concern about coupling test initialization to module load order / persistent mock state is diff-grounded. However, the diff alone doesn’t prove this causes a failing/incorrect test run, so it’s more a test-structure/maintainability issue than a verified defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Permission escalation via OR-union of two ability sources in AlertRuleMenu.tsx and RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx: canDelete unions folder-metadata and ruler API authorization sources, resolving disagreements to the most permissive answer for destructive actions; should be intersection or exclusively selected

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes authorization gating to an OR-union of two independent ability sources. In AlertRuleMenu.tsx, canPause/canDelete/canDuplicate/canSilence/canExport are computed as `(rulerSupported && rulerAllowed) || (grafanaSupported && grafanaAllowed)`, after fetching both `useRulerRuleAbilities(...)` and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(...)`. In RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx, `canEditRule` is similarly computed as an OR between `useRulerRuleAbility(...)` and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility(...)`. This means if the two sources disagree (e.g., one says not allowed), the UI will still enable/show the action based on the more permissive answer, which is a real permission/authorization defect in the client-side RBAC logic for destructive/modifying actions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Federated-rule protection silently dropped: useAllAlertRuleAbilities hardcodes isFederated = false with a TODO, making federated Mimir rule groups fully editable/deletable (regression from old isFederatedRuleGroup check)

adjudication.rationale: In `useAbilities.ts`, federated-rule immutability is effectively removed: `useAllRulerRuleAbilities()` now sets `isFederated = false` (with a TODO) instead of using the prior `isFederatedRuleGroup(...)` check, and `useAllAlertRuleAbilities()` (now deprecated) delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities()`. Since `immutableRule` is computed as `isProvisioned || isFederated || isPluginProvided`, hardcoding `isFederated` to false means federated groups will no longer be treated as immutable and may become editable/deletable if `useIsRuleEditable` returns true.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Ruler/prom reconciliation deleted in GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx: ruler-only rules (creating state) disappear from list, and prom-only rules (being deleted) render as normal rules with full Edit/Delete menus

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the ruler/prom reconciliation logic in `GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx`: it no longer calls `useGetGrafanaRulerGroupQuery`, deletes `matchRules`, and now renders only `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules` as `GrafanaRuleListItem`. This means the UI can no longer represent the previous special states for (a) ruler-only rules (previously rendered with `RuleOperation.Creating`) and (b) prom-only rules (previously rendered as `RuleOperationListItem` with `RuleOperation.Deleting`). However, whether those out-of-sync states still occur is not verifiable from the diff alone (the removed code even commented they "should be strongly consistent now"), so this is best treated as an edge-case/assumption regression concern rather than a guaranteed defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Tests covering creating/deleting states and matchRules in GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx were deleted, not migrated, removing coverage that would catch the reconciliation regression

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the reconciliation logic in `GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx` (no more `useGetGrafanaRulerGroupQuery`, `matchRules`, `promOnlyRules`, or creating/deleting `RuleOperationListItem` rendering) and correspondingly deletes the `matchRules` unit tests plus the prior creating/deleting state tests in `GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx`, replacing them with menu/action RBAC tests. This does eliminate coverage that previously validated handling of prom-only/ruler-only mismatches; if that mismatch can still occur, there’s now no test guarding it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Rules without a folderUid are silently stripped of all edit/delete permissions in useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable: missing folderUid returns isEditable:false with loading:false, indistinguishable from a permission denial with no error surfaced

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable` and it explicitly returns `{ isEditable:false, isRemovable:false, loading:false }` when `!rule || !folderUID` (where `folderUID = rule?.folderUid`). That makes a missing/empty `folderUid` indistinguishable from a real permission denial and does not surface any error. However, `GrafanaPromRuleDTOBase` in the diff still types `folderUid` as a required `string`, so whether this can happen at runtime isn’t verifiable from the diff alone—this is an edge-case/robustness concern rather than a proven functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Folder-metadata permission check (hasPermissionInMetadata) in useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable may deny org-level or basic-role AlertingRuleUpdate grants that have no per-folder metadata entry; the new test only passes because the mock explicitly injects folder access control metadata

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable()` which determines `isEditable`/`isRemovable` via folder metadata checks only: `ctx.hasPermissionInMetadata(rulesPermissions.update, folder)` and `...delete...` (new code in `useAbilities.ts`). The updated tests for Grafana rules explicitly inject folder ACL metadata via `setFolderAccessControl(...)` to make edit/delete/actions appear. From the diff alone, it’s not provable that org-level/basic-role grants are *not* reflected in `folder` metadata (that depends on `ctx.hasPermissionInMetadata` / folder model not shown), so it’s not a confirmed defect; however, the finding is a concrete, diff-grounded concern about a newly introduced permission-checking approach potentially narrowing behavior and being test-dependent on injected metadata.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx returns null for any non-Grafana prom-only rule: getEditableIdentifier fails and the entire action row silently renders nothing, with logWarning going to analytics rather than the user

adjudication.rationale: In RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx, getEditableIdentifier() returns undefined unless either (a) a RulerRuleDTO `rule` is provided or (b) `promRule` is a Grafana Prom rule (`prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule)`). The component then does `if (!identifier) { return null; }`, and only logs via `logWarning('Unable to construct an editable rule identifier')`, providing no UI fallback. This is a real diff-grounded edge-case/silent failure risk introduced by broadening props to allow promRule-only usage, but the diff does not show any concrete call site passing a non-Grafana prom-only rule, so it’s not verifiable as an actual broken behavior in this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Loading-state race on Silence ability in useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities: no loading gating on the Silence tuple, so the menu item can flicker in/out and a not-yet-settled prom-side check can enable Silence for unsupported rules

adjudication.rationale: In `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, most abilities are gated via `MaybeSupported = loading ? NotSupported : AlwaysSupported`, but `AlertRuleAction.Silence` is computed as `[silenceSupported, canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule]` without referencing `loading` (or the immutable/provisioned gating used elsewhere). This is a diff-grounded inconsistency that could lead to transient UI changes as `useFolder(...)`/permission-derived state settles, though the diff alone doesn’t prove it will incorrectly enable Silence for unsupported rules (it is still gated by `isAlertingRule`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: returnTo query param dropped from rule view links in GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx, breaking back-navigation context from the list view

adjudication.rationale: In the deleted GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx, GrafanaRuleListItem built the rule view link as `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })` where `returnTo` came from `createReturnTo()`. In the new GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx, the href is now `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`)` with no `returnTo` param. This is a verifiable behavioral change in link generation that can break the preserved back-navigation context from the list view.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test-side meta-issue: all ability hooks are jest.mocked wholesale with both sources mocked to the same values, making the OR-union logic, ability-source disagreement, and undefined-folder/no-folderUid paths structurally untestable

adjudication.rationale: In `RulesTable.test.tsx` the entire `../../hooks/useAbilities` module is mocked (`jest.mock('../../hooks/useAbilities')`), and the new multi-source OR-union behavior introduced in `AlertRuleMenu.tsx` (combining `useRulerRuleAbilities` and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`) and `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx` (combining `useRulerRuleAbility` with `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility`) is not actually exercised by these tests. The default mocks return identical `[false,false]` tuples for both sources, and the per-test overrides generally set permissions in a single consistent direction rather than creating a “source disagreement” case (e.g., ruler denies but prom allows) that would validate the OR logic. Also, since the hooks are mocked wholesale, the newly added internal paths in `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` / `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable` (e.g., `!rule`/`!folderUid`/missing folder) are bypassed and therefore untested in this test file.
